title: Gospel of John
author: john-evangelist
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to John the Evangelist. The text itself is anonymous, and its authorship is disputed in modern scholarship. The traditional attribution is labelled as such.
description: The Fourth Gospel opens with a poetic prologue identifying the Word (Logos) with God and with the light entering the world. This sample presents the prologue's first five verses.
historicalContext: John is generally dated to the late first or early second century and reflects a community in dialogue with Jewish and emerging Christian traditions. Its Logos language also resonates with Greek philosophical vocabulary.

editions.title: Greek New Testament text (Wikisource transcription)
editions.attributionText: Greek text of the Gospel of John, Wikisource transcription of a public-domain edition. Punctuation and orthography follow the source.
editions.notes: Original-language excerpt; not a critical edition.

texts.1.1: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν Θεόν, καὶ Θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος.
texts.1.2: οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν.
texts.1.3: πάντα δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο οὐδὲ ἕν ὃ γέγονεν.
texts.1.4: ἐν αὐτῷ ζωὴ ἦν, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἦν τὸ φῶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων,
texts.1.5: καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει, καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν.

editions.title: The Holy Bible, King James Version
editions.attributionText: The Holy Bible, King James Version (1611). Public domain. Text from Project Gutenberg eBook #10.
editions.notes: Public-domain translation. Early modern spelling and punctuation are retained.

texts.1.1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
texts.1.2: The same was in the beginning with God.
texts.1.3: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
texts.1.4: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
texts.1.5: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
